justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: online claim submission and processing are addressed via Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace and Claims Core Engine, while claim-type migration is managed by Claim Type Feature Flags Component and Feature Router Component.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Adjuster sub-2s latency is met using Next.js SSR / API Routes Component and Resilience & Caching Proxy, isolating 5s mainframe latencies via asynchronous Azure Service Bus messaging and Polyglot Persistence Layer.
justifications.compatibility: The Integration Mediator and Copybook Mapper Component bridge modern JSON payloads to legacy COBOL copybooks over TCP/MQ. Token Validator Component in Azure API Management integrates with Active Directory.
justifications.usability: Distinct user personas are well catered for: external brokers and adjusters interact through Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace, while migration leads use the dedicated Migration Operations Dashboard.
justifications.reliability: Zero loss and exactly-once processing are protected by Azure Service Bus Dead-Letter Subscriptions, Circuit Breaker & Retry Policy Component, Managed CDC & Audit Streamer, and Reconciliation Processor.
justifications.security: Active Directory SSO is directly enforced at the perimeter via Token Validator Component using OAuth2/OIDC policies, supported by TLS encryption and Row-Level Security in Operations Datastore.
justifications.maintainability: One-day rollback is enabled via Claim Type Feature Flags Component, Dynamic Routing Policy Engine, and Feature Router Component using Azure App Configuration, with an anti-corruption layer in Integration Mediator.
justifications.portability: The hybrid topology between on-premise mainframe and Azure West Europe is well-modeled, though high coupling to Azure-native services (Logic Apps, Cosmos DB, Azure App Configuration) restricts future cloud replaceability.

PERF-01.justification: BFF server-side rendering, Resilience4j caching proxy, and local persistence decouple adjuster reads from the mainframe. However, cache-miss latency for legacy-resident fields could exceed 2 seconds without explicit prefetching.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio for open claims with mainframe-resident data
Fallback response time during circuit breaker trips
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of cached adjuster claim data versus real-time mainframe accuracy

PERF-02.justification: Azure Service Bus and Enterprise Messaging Queue buffer submission spikes. The asynchronous decoupling ensures burst traffic is ingested without increasing real-time mainframe load or violating batch windows.
sensitivity_points: Service bus queue ingestion capacity and throttling limits
Batch window scheduling policy to pause egress dispatch
tradeoffs: Customer submission confirmation acknowledgment versus delayed core mainframe processing

AVAIL-01.justification: Online submissions are buffered in Azure Service Bus and staged in persistence. Integration Mediator's circuit breaker and retries defer mainframe synchronization until after the batch window finishes.
sensitivity_points: Message retention duration in Azure Service Bus during batch windows
Backpressure and rate limiting when forwarding messages post-window
tradeoffs: Asynchronous intake availability versus delayed claim confirmation in the legacy system of record

AVAIL-02.justification: Transactional persistence in PostgreSQL, managed CDC via Event Hubs, Dead-Letter queues, and a dedicated Reconciliation Processor ensure failed synchronizations are caught, audited, and safely reconciled without duplicates.
elements: Managed CDC & Audit Streamer (Azure Event Hubs)
sensitivity_points: Idempotency enforcement across copybook transactions and message consumers
Lag in CDC streaming to the reconciliation processor
tradeoffs: Operational overhead of dead-letter triage versus strict zero-data-loss guarantee

MOD-01.justification: Feature flagging via Azure App Configuration in APIM, the BFF, and Claims Core Engine allows dynamic routing and instantaneous switch-back within a day without redeployments.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency of feature flag updates across distributed components
Dual-write synchronization fidelity prior to rollback
tradeoffs: Architectural complexity of feature toggles across layers versus operational switch-back speed

MOD-02.justification: The Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace communicate exclusively through Azure API Management and the Claims Core Engine. Legacy integration is fully isolated behind the Integration Mediator, requiring no UI rewrites.
sensitivity_points: Completeness of domain data migration in Polyglot Persistence Layer
Decoupling of BFF APIs from legacy mainframe schemas
tradeoffs: Upfront cost of Anti-Corruption Layer versus effortless retirement of legacy mainframe

SEC-01.justification: APIM validates tokens against Active Directory, and Row-Level Security exists in the Operations Datastore. However, fine-grained multi-tenant domain authorization to restrict broker access to specific claims is not explicitly modeled in Claims Core Engine.
sensitivity_points: Fine-grained claims-based authorization logic within the Claims Core Engine
Audit logging completeness for unauthorized access attempts
tradeoffs: Gateway-level validation efficiency versus defense-in-depth resource-level access enforcement

SEC-02.justification: Single sign-on via Active Directory and APIM Token Validator enables centralized revocation. However, short access token expiry (under 15 minutes) or explicit token revocation checks are not explicitly documented.
sensitivity_points: Availability of instant token introspection or revocation mechanisms in APIM
tradeoffs: Short-lived token validation overhead versus strict adherence to the 15-minute revocation window
